title: Free Sample Packet Tavern
theme: Lively fantasy tavern with a private room, two guest rooms, a busy kitchen, and a hidden coin stash
hook: Harkwin Volberg's warm common room is full of travelers, gossip, and small trouble. The Game Master can use the tavern as a starting scene, a safe stop between adventures, or a compact social location with one hidden prize.
background: Volberg's Tavern is a cozy roadside house where meals are hot, beds are scarce, and business is usually handled by the hearth. Harkwin Volberg keeps order with good humor and a heavy serving ladle, but he also hides his strongbox coin in a false stone beside the fireplace. Tonight the tavern can host a negotiation, a rumor trade, a missing guest, or a quiet search for the stash before someone less friendly finds it.

layout.notes: Single-floor tavern centered on the common room, with short interior routes to kitchen, guest rooms, storage, and private meeting space.

rooms.name: Lobby/Common Room
rooms.readAloud: Warm firelight rolls across crowded tables, polished mugs, and a long hearth of honey-colored stone. Harkwin Volberg laughs behind the bar while travelers trade rumors over stew and dark ale.
rooms.gmNotes: This is the social hub. Harkwin knows who entered each rented room, who requested privacy, and which patron has been asking too many questions about the hearth stones.

inhabitants.name: Harkwin Volberg
inhabitants.tactics: Uses charm first, then a ladle, chair, or shouted call for help
inhabitants.morale: Protects the tavern but avoids needless bloodshed
inhabitants.wants: A peaceful evening and his hidden savings left alone
inhabitants.leverage: He trades rumors for help calming trouble discreetly

inhabitants.name: Tired Road Patrons
inhabitants.tactics: Duck under tables, shout accusations, or block exits by accident
inhabitants.wants: Food, warmth, and no trouble near their paid mugs
inhabitants.leverage: A round of drinks loosens useful details

rooms.treasure: Volberg's coin stash sits behind a fake stone beside the fireplace. It holds the tavern savings, several stamped trade tokens, and a small silver brooch left as collateral.
rooms.secrets: The false hearth stone can be noticed by soot-free edges, a hollow sound, or Harkwin glancing toward it whenever money is mentioned.
rooms.exits: Interior doors lead to the kitchen, both guest bedrooms, the storage room, and the private meeting room.

rooms.name: Kitchen Area
rooms.readAloud: The kitchen is bright, hot, and fragrant with onions, pepper, and fresh bread. Copper pots hang over a worktable dusted with flour.
rooms.gmNotes: The kitchen staff hears most common-room conversations through the serving hatch. A hurried chase can spill soup, knock down hanging pans, or reveal a hidden message tucked under the bread board.

inhabitants.name: Mara the Cook
inhabitants.tactics: Throws flour, slams doors, and calls for Harkwin
inhabitants.morale: Stands firm if the tavern is threatened
inhabitants.wants: Her kitchen respected and no muddy boots near the oven
inhabitants.leverage: She will talk if asked politely away from the crowd

rooms.treasure: A jar of good spice, two bottles of pear brandy, and a clean iron key ring for the pantry shelves.
rooms.secrets: Mara saw a private-room guest pass a wax-sealed note to someone sleeping in Room 3.
rooms.exits: Doorway back to the common room.

rooms.name: Guest Bedroom: Roadside Room
rooms.readAloud: A narrow bed, a wash basin, and a travel chest fill this snug rented room. A small window looks toward the road.
rooms.gmNotes: This room works as a quiet interview space, a search scene, or a place for a tired patron to hide. The window latch squeaks unless lifted carefully.
rooms.treasure: A forgotten purse with a few local coins may be found under the bed if the room has not been cleaned yet.
rooms.secrets: A folded scrap under the mattress lists three names and the phrase "after the second bell."
rooms.exits: Door back to the common room.

structuredExits.label: Route to Room 1
structuredExits.description: Door back to the common room.

rooms.name: Guest Bedroom: Hearthside Room
rooms.readAloud: This rented room smells faintly of smoke and lavender soap. A heavy quilt covers the bed, and boot prints mark the floorboards near the door.
rooms.gmNotes: Use this room for a missing guest, an overheard argument, or a sleeping witness who knows more than they admit.

inhabitants.name: Dozing Peddler
inhabitants.tactics: Stalls, complains, and tries to keep their goods out of sight
inhabitants.wants: To avoid being blamed for someone else’s deal
inhabitants.leverage: They remember voices but want privacy before speaking

rooms.treasure: A travel bundle contains mundane trade goods, mending thread, and one brass whistle.
rooms.secrets: Mud on the boot prints matches the alley behind the tavern rather than the front road.
rooms.exits: Door back to the common room.

structuredExits.label: Route to Room 1
structuredExits.description: Door back to the common room.

rooms.name: Storage Room
rooms.readAloud: Crates of turnips, ale casks, spare blankets, and rolled rush mats crowd this little room. The smell is dry wood, old apples, and cellar dust.
rooms.gmNotes: Volberg sometimes lets an extra patron sleep here. It is cramped, easy to search, and useful for hiding a person, parcel, or eavesdropper.
rooms.treasure: A practical supply cache: candles, rope, blankets, lamp oil, and a small keg of sour but drinkable ale.
rooms.secrets: A loose crate lid hides a wrapped cloak and a sealed note meant for the private meeting room.
rooms.exits: Door back to the common room.

structuredExits.label: Route to Room 1
structuredExits.description: Door back to the common room.

rooms.name: Private Meeting Room
rooms.readAloud: A small table, four sturdy chairs, and a shuttered side window make this room feel quieter than the tavern around it. The walls soften the common-room noise to a low murmur.
rooms.gmNotes: This is the best place for bargains, rumors, threats, or secret hiring. If trouble starts here, patrons in the common room hear raised voices but not exact words.

inhabitants.name: Cloaked Negotiator
inhabitants.threat: Low alone, Moderate with hired guards
inhabitants.tactics: Offers payment, withholds names, and leaves through the common room if pressed
inhabitants.wants: A discreet message delivered before dawn
inhabitants.leverage: They know why someone is asking about Volberg’s hearth

rooms.treasure: A locked writing case may hold contracts, a local map scrap, or payment for a small errand.
rooms.secrets: The shutters hide a narrow viewing gap toward the road, useful for watching who approaches the tavern.
rooms.exits: Door back to the common room.

treasureTable.result: Volberg’s hidden coin pouch from the false hearth stone
Stamped trade tokens accepted at nearby roadside inns
Silver brooch left as collateral by a nervous traveler

Practical tavern supplies useful for travel: candles, rope, blankets, and lamp oil

gmNotes: Use this packet as a quick complete sample: start with a rumor, a missing guest, or a quiet search for the hidden hearth stash.
Keep the tone warm and lively unless the table pushes toward danger.
The player map should never reveal the hidden coin cache or GM-only markers.
The tavern is intentionally compact: most play flows through the common room, then branches to one or two side rooms.
